summary: This initiative carries exactly one surviving finding (speculative-generality-0011) proposing the deletion of three uncalled exports from packages/core: nearestPixelWithin (geometry/pixel-grid.ts:128), assertTriggerGraphIntegrity (voice/graph-integrity.ts:218) and listCanvasScenes (canvas/registry.ts:33). The right-sized design is three independent deletions plus one test rewrite — no abstraction, no new seam, no relocation. The only real design decision is ORDER and EVIDENCE, because two of the three exports are reachable through core's public barrels (`export * from './canvas/registry'` at src/index.ts:33 and `export * as voice from './voice'` at src/index.ts:73, whose voice/index.ts:18 blanket-exports graph-integrity), and one of them (assertTriggerGraphIntegrity) is a *validation* surface that a 2026-07-08 PRD explicitly specified as intended public API. So the plan: (1) freeze a machine-checkable no-caller proof before touching anything, since a green suite proves nothing about symbols with zero callers; (2) make the pixel-grid test independent of the wrapper BEFORE deleting the wrapper, so the deletion commit is a pure subtraction that typecheck alone can validate; (3) delete the three functions in three separately-revertable commits, gated on Trent's answer for the guard-shaped one; (4) re-measure the package's runtime export surface to prove the trim removed exactly what it claimed and orphaned nothing. Synthesis changed the EVIDENCE INSTRUMENTS, not the shape: the opus plan's two runtime measurements were both unexecutable or vacuous as written (a `dist/index.js` import against a package that never builds a dist, and a knip unused-export claim that knip does not actually make about any of the three symbols — measured, not assumed). They are replaced by a tsx namespace-key count that was RUN in this worktree (top-level 159, voice 64 at HEAD 8b5af91 → expected 158 / 63 after the trim) plus executable dynamic-access regexes with a verified positive control. Deliberately NOT in scope: the voice barrel's blanket re-exports (middle-man finding, unassigned to any initiative) and any un-exporting of validateTriggerGraphIntegrity — narrowing a barrel is a different, larger argument than deleting a dead function, and folding it in here would turn a 30-line subtraction into a cross-package export audit.

design.title: Freeze the no-caller proof and the measured baselines
design.intent: Deleting an export whose only defence is 'nobody calls it' needs the no-caller claim recorded as reproducible machine output at the commit that removes it, because no test can go red for a symbol with zero call sites. This step changes no source; it produces the evidence artifact the three deletion commits cite, and it is the step that would ABORT the initiative if any dynamic or string-keyed access is found. It also freezes the three numbers every later gate compares against (test count, top-level export count, voice namespace count), because the plan-level 2968 figure is stale.
design.verification: Record verbatim output of, at repo root, all six of the following. (a) LITERAL SCAN: `rg -n 'nearestPixelWithin|assertTriggerGraphIntegrity|listCanvasScenes' -g '!node_modules' -g '!dist' -g '!docs/plans/2026-07-26-deep-review'` — expected EXACTLY nine hits, verified at HEAD 8b5af91: packages/core/src/geometry/pixel-grid.ts:128; packages/core/src/geometry/pixel-grid.test.ts:4 (import), :80 (the `it(...)` title string), :84 (call), :129 (call); packages/core/src/canvas/registry.ts:33; packages/core/src/voice/graph-integrity.ts:218; docs/reports/2026-07-05-elv2-u5-report.md:111 (prose, a rejected alternative in a dated report); docs/plans/2026-07-08-gen3-graph-authoring-stabilisation-prd.md:104 (prose signature). NOTE the :80 test-title hit — the opus plan's expected list omitted it, which would have fired a spurious ABORT. (b) DYNAMIC-ACCESS SCAN, one fully single-quoted command so no shell escaping can silently mangle it: `rg -n '["\x27`](nearestPixelWithin|assertTriggerGraphIntegrity|listCanvasScenes)["\x27`]' -g '!node_modules' -g '!docs'` — the `\x27` is the single quote, so the class covers obj['x'], obj["x"], obj[`x`] and string-keyed map lookups in one pass. Verified at HEAD: exit 1, zero output. Verified to actually fire against a synthetic control file containing `m['listCanvasScenes']` and ``m[`assertTriggerGraphIntegrity`]`` — record that control run in the evidence file so the gate is proven non-vacuous rather than merely quiet. (c) NO EXTERNAL CONSUMER: `rg -n '"private"' packages/core/package.json` showing `"private": true`; plus `rg -n '@ledrums/core/' apps packages -g '!node_modules'` returning nothing (no deep imports bypassing the barrel). (d) RUNTIME SURFACE BASELINE: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec tsx -e "import('@ledrums/core').then(m=>{console.log('TOP',Object.keys(m).length);console.log('VOICE',Object.keys(m.voice).length)})"` — RUN in this worktree at HEAD 8b5af91, prints `TOP 159` / `VOICE 64`. Record both numbers as TOP_BASE and VOICE_BASE. (e) TEST BASELINE: run `pnpm gates` and record the collected test count as BASELINE_TESTS. Do NOT reuse the 2968 figure from the Phase 0 baseline sha 3708648 — fix batches 1-3 landed after it and `git diff --stat 3708648..HEAD -- '*.test.ts'` shows seven test files changed including packages/core/src/geometry/mirror.test.ts deleted outright (-136 lines), so 2968 no longer holds. (f) KNIP BASELINE, recorded as a regression fingerprint only: `pnpm -w exec knip --workspace packages/core --include exports --reporter json`. MEASURED at HEAD: `{"issues":[]}` — knip reports NONE of the three symbols, because package.json maps `exports['.']` to src/index.ts so every barrel-reachable name is public API to knip, and nearestPixelWithin has a live consumer in its own test file. Knip therefore CANNOT confirm this finding and must not be cited as if it did; it is kept solely so S6 can prove no NEW orphan appeared. Also record the whole-repo fingerprint `pnpm -w exec knip --include exports --reporter json`, measured at HEAD as exactly two files: apps/web/src/lib/app/patch-topology.ts (STAGE_ORDER, triggerId, zoneNodeId, outputId) and apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store/graph-wiring.ts (reaches). ABORT the initiative and re-file if (a) returns any hit outside the nine listed, or if (b) returns anything at all.
design.reverses: Delete the evidence file; no source changed.

design.title: Rewrite pixel-grid tests onto nearestPixelIdWithin
design.intent: packages/core/src/geometry/pixel-grid.test.ts is the wrapper's only consumer, and what it actually proves is brute-force equivalence of the spatial hash — a property the id-returning primitive establishes on its own. Moving the two assertions onto nearestPixelIdWithin removes the last caller without weakening the test, so the subsequent deletion is provably caller-free rather than caller-free-because-we-deleted-the-caller.
design.verification: In test 'nearestPixelWithin matches the brute-force nearest scan (confetti equivalence)' (line 80), rename it to 'nearestPixelIdWithin matches the brute-force nearest scan (confetti equivalence)', replace `const hit = nearestPixelWithin(grid, pt, reach)` (line 84) with `const id = nearestPixelIdWithin(grid, pt, reach)`, and replace the three assertions with: `expect(id).toBe(-1)` when `brute.dist > reach`; otherwise `expect(id).toBe(brute.id)` AND `expect(distance(m.pixels[id]!.world, pt)).toBeCloseTo(brute.dist, 10)` — the distance assertion MUST be kept (recomputed via `distance`, already imported at line 5 from '../math'), because dropping it would silently reduce coverage under cover of a refactor. In 'handles an empty model' (line 129) replace `expect(nearestPixelWithin(g, {x:0,y:0,z:0}, 100)).toBeNull()` with `expect(nearestPixelIdWithin(g, {x:0,y:0,z:0}, 100)).toBe(-1)`. Update the import on line 4 to `{ buildPixelGrid, forEachPixelWithin, nearestPixelIdWithin }`. Verify: `pnpm gates` green at exactly BASELINE_TESTS from S1 (the rewrite adds and removes no test); `git diff --stat` shows exactly one file, tests only, zero production lines; and re-run S1(d), which must still print TOP 159 / VOICE 64 (a test-only change cannot move the runtime surface). Additionally re-run S1(f) scoped to packages/core and record the result as DATA, NOT A GATE: removing the wrapper's only importer may cause knip to begin reporting nearestPixelWithin as an unused export, which would be a welcome bonus confirmation — but knip staying silent is NOT an abort condition, because S1(f) already measured that knip's entry model does not classify these symbols.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit; the wrapper still exists at this point, so the old assertions compile unchanged.

design.title: Delete nearestPixelWithin from pixel-grid.ts
design.intent: Remove the object-returning convenience (pixel-grid.ts:127-136) that undoes the allocation-free contract its own neighbour documents ('no closure, no result object — safe on a per-particle-per-frame hot path'). The module keeps one nearest-query shape instead of two, and the hot-path contract stops having a documented escape hatch nobody took.
design.verification: Delete lines 127-136 (the `/** Object-returning convenience over {@link nearestPixelIdWithin}. */` doc plus the function; verified at HEAD that 127 is the doc line and 136 the closing brace). Confirm `distance` (imported at line 2 from '../math') is STILL used by forEachPixelWithin and nearestPixelIdWithin — `rg -n 'distance\(' packages/core/src/geometry/pixel-grid.ts` must return ≥2 hits, otherwise remove the now-dead import. pixel-grid is NOT re-exported from packages/core/src/index.ts (verified: `rg -n 'pixel-grid' packages/core/src/index.ts` returns nothing, exit 1), so no barrel edit is required — assert this with that same command. Then `pnpm gates` green at BASELINE_TESTS. Re-run S1(d): TOP and VOICE must be UNCHANGED at 159/64, because this symbol was never on the package surface — a change here would mean the deletion hit the wrong thing. Because the four production consumers (effects/impl/confetti-burst.ts, rain-3d.ts, spark-arc.ts, lightning.ts) call nearestPixelIdWithin/forEachPixelWithin and not the wrapper, a clean `pnpm typecheck` is a complete proof of no broken caller here.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit — a pure 10-line re-addition with no other file's state depending on it.

design.title: Delete assertTriggerGraphIntegrity (guard-shaped: gated on Trent)
design.intent: graph-integrity.ts:218-223 is a throwing wrapper over validateTriggerGraphIntegrity with zero callers including tests, in a module whose actual policy is to return coded issues as data (`issues[]`). Deleting it collapses the module to one validation shape, so no future caller has to decide between two policies. This is the one step that removes a (never-reached) failure path, so it is fenced behind an explicit human confirmation rather than merged with the mechanical trims.
design.verification: PRECONDITION: open_question 'throwing-form-intent' answered by Trent — the 2026-07-08 Gen3 PRD (docs/plans/2026-07-08-gen3-graph-authoring-stabilisation-prd.md:104) specified this exact signature as intended public API, so the no-caller evidence alone does not settle intent. ON 'DELETE': remove lines 218-223 (verified at HEAD: 218 is the `export function assertTriggerGraphIntegrity` line, 223 the closing brace). validateTriggerGraphIntegrity and normalizeTriggerGraphToGen3 stay untouched — assert with `rg -n 'export function' packages/core/src/voice/graph-integrity.ts` returning exactly those two. Do NOT edit packages/core/src/voice/index.ts:18 (`export * from './graph-integrity'`) — narrowing that barrel is out of scope for this initiative. Verify `pnpm gates` green at BASELINE_TESTS; re-run the S1(a) literal scan to confirm the symbol now appears only in the two prose docs; and re-run S1(d), where VOICE must drop by exactly 1 (64 → 63) with TOP unchanged, since the symbol lives under the `voice` namespace object and not the top-level barrel. ON 'KEEP': make NO source change in this step. Record Trent's intent answer verbatim in the evidence file and in 04-ledger.json, mark speculative-generality-0011 partially-retired (two of three symbols), and file a follow-up ticket to wire the intended caller on the graph-import/authoring validation path — that wiring is explicitly OUT of this initiative's scope and must not be attempted here. (The opus plan's 'keep' branch said both 'skip this step' and 'add a caller in the same change'; no such caller exists or is designed anywhere, so that instruction was unexecutable and is removed.) On 'keep', S6's expected VOICE count stays at 64.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit restores the 6-line throwing wrapper verbatim; nothing else references it, so the revert is total and order-independent with respect to S3/S5.

design.title: Delete listCanvasScenes from canvas/registry.ts
design.intent: registry.ts:33-35 exists only to complete a CRUD quartet (register/unregister/tryGet/list). The web reads scenes from its own store (store.allCanvasScenes), and core's resolve path is tryGetCanvasEffect. Deleting it removes an enumeration of module-private mutable state from core's PUBLIC barrel, which is the largest single interface reduction in this initiative — `export * from './canvas/registry'` at src/index.ts:33 means this symbol is currently part of @ledrums/core's top-level surface.
design.verification: Delete lines 33-35 (verified at HEAD). The module-private `scenes` Map must remain used by registerCanvasScene/unregisterCanvasScene/tryGetCanvasScene/tryGetCanvasEffect — `rg -n 'scenes\.' packages/core/src/canvas/registry.ts` must return ≥5 hits, proving no dead state is left behind. Leave packages/core/src/index.ts:33 as-is (the wildcard now exports one fewer name; no line edit needed). Verify `pnpm gates` green at BASELINE_TESTS; `rg -n 'listCanvasScenes' apps packages -g '!node_modules'` returns nothing; and re-run S1(d), where TOP must drop by exactly 1 (159 → 158) with VOICE unchanged. That count is the load-bearing check for this step — it is the only direct runtime evidence that the deletion actually shrank the package surface by the one name claimed and no other. Note docs/reports/2026-07-05-elv2-u5-report.md:111 mentions the symbol only as a rejected alternative in a dated report — a historical record, not live documentation, so it is deliberately not edited.
design.reverses: `git revert` this commit; the 3-line accessor is restored over unchanged module state.

design.title: Re-measure the export surface and close the evidence loop
design.intent: Prove the trim did what it claimed and created nothing new: no orphaned imports, no newly-unused private helper exposed by the deletions, and the interface delta actually equals the symbols claimed. This is what turns 'the suite is still green' (which it would be even if we had deleted the wrong thing, since these symbols had no tests) into positive evidence.
design.verification: Append to the evidence file, on the merged HEAD: (a) RUNTIME SURFACE DELTA — re-run S1(d) verbatim (`pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec tsx -e "import('@ledrums/core').then(m=>{console.log('TOP',Object.keys(m).length);console.log('VOICE',Object.keys(m.voice).length)})"`, confirmed executable in this worktree). Expected `TOP 158` / `VOICE 63` if S4 ran on 'delete'; `TOP 158` / `VOICE 64` if S4 was answered 'keep'. Any other pair means a deletion removed more or less than the named symbol — STOP and report. This command REPLACES the opus plan's `pnpm build` + `node -e "import('./packages/core/dist/index.js')"` check, which could never have run: packages/core's build script is `tsc --noEmit` and its exports field is `".": "./src/index.ts"`, so no dist/index.js is ever produced. Do NOT add a build step to core for this. (b) NO-NEW-ORPHANS REGRESSION — re-run both knip commands from S1(f) and diff against the recorded fingerprint. The gate is one-directional: any NEW entry under packages/core (for a symbol other than the three deleted names) means a deletion orphaned a private helper — STOP and remove it too. Knip failing to list the deleted symbols proves nothing either way and must not be recorded as confirmation; S1(f) already measured that knip's entry model treats barrel-reachable names as public API. (c) `rg -n 'nearestPixelWithin|assertTriggerGraphIntegrity|listCanvasScenes' -g '!node_modules' -g '!docs'` returning nothing across all source (the two remaining hits are prose docs, excluded here deliberately). (d) final `pnpm gates` green at BASELINE_TESTS. Any deviation from the expected deltas is a defect in this plan, not a rounding error — stop and report.

interface_deltas.at: packages/core/src/geometry/pixel-grid.ts (module-internal; not in the package barrel)
interface_deltas.note: Two nearest-query shapes collapse to one; the allocation-free hot-path contract loses its documented escape hatch. Package-external surface unchanged because pixel-grid is imported by relative path only — verified: `rg 'pixel-grid' packages/core/src/index.ts` is empty, and the runtime top-level key count is unchanged by S3 (159 → 159).

Removes a second, throwing validation policy from a module whose contract is issues-as-data. Measured: the voice namespace object has 64 keys at HEAD and 63 after this deletion. Conditional on Trent answering 'delete'. The voice barrel's blanket re-export line stays — narrowing it belongs to the unassigned voice-barrel middle-man finding, not here.
The only change that shrinks @ledrums/core's top-level export set; removes public enumeration of module-private mutable registry state. Measured: 159 top-level keys at HEAD, 158 after.

checks: `pnpm gates` green after each of S2, S3, S4, S5 and on the final merged HEAD — the collected test count must equal BASELINE_TESTS as recorded in S1 at the pre-deletion HEAD, in every run (a changed count means a test was added, deleted or renamed into/out of existence, which this plan forbids). BASELINE_TESTS is measured in S1, NOT taken as 2968: that figure was collected at Phase 0 sha 3708648, and fix batches 1-3 have since landed, deleting packages/core/src/geometry/mirror.test.ts outright among seven changed test files.

`pnpm typecheck` (inside gates) is the PRIMARY parity instrument for S3/S4/S5: for a deleted symbol with zero call sites, a clean compile of packages/core + apps/server + apps/web + packages/io is a total proof that no STATIC caller broke, since the whole workspace is TypeScript and @ledrums/core is `private: true` with no external consumer and no deep-path importers.

The runtime namespace-key count, run before (S1) and after (S6) via `pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec tsx -e "import('@ledrums/core')..."` — measured 159 top-level / 64 voice at HEAD 8b5af91, expected 158 / 63 after the full trim. This is the only check that positively measures the interface reduction rather than merely failing to contradict it, and it is the check the opus plan lacked (its dist-import form was unrunnable against a package whose build is `tsc --noEmit`).

S1's frozen `rg` output — the literal nine-hit scan plus the quote-class dynamic-access scan `rg -n '["\x27`](nearestPixelWithin|assertTriggerGraphIntegrity|listCanvasScenes)["\x27`]'`, which was verified BOTH to return nothing at HEAD and to fire against a synthetic control containing bracket access in single-quote and backtick form. A guard that has never been seen to fire is not evidence; this one has.

Knip is a NO-NEW-ORPHANS regression fingerprint only, never a confirmation. Measured at HEAD: `knip --workspace packages/core --include exports` returns `{"issues":[]}` and the whole-repo run flags only apps/web patch-topology.ts and graph-wiring.ts. It does not and cannot flag the three target symbols, because src/index.ts is an entry point via the package's `exports` field and nearestPixelWithin has a consumer in its own test file.

S2-specific: the two rewritten assertions still compare against `bruteNearest` AND still assert the distance to 10 decimal places, so the equivalence property under test is byte-identical in strength; diff review must confirm no `expect` was dropped.

S3-specific: `rg -n 'nearestPixelIdWithin|forEachPixelWithin|buildPixelGrid' packages/core/src/effects/` still shows confetti-burst.ts, rain-3d.ts, spark-arc.ts and lightning.ts as callers — verified at HEAD; the module's live consumers are untouched by the trim.

Render-loop smoke (S6, non-model evidence): run the app with `LEDRUMS_ENGINE=voice pnpm dev`, fire the four grid-consuming effects (confetti-burst, rain-3d, spark-arc, lightning) from TriggerLab, and confirm pixel output renders with no console errors — covers the one region where a mistaken deletion would show up as silence rather than a red test.
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps: A green suite cannot prove anything about symbols that had zero callers — that is precisely why they are being deleted, and it means S4 and S5 would pass identically whether or not the deletion was correct. Four specific gaps, and what replaces the suite in each: (1) assertTriggerGraphIntegrity is a validation surface a PRD specified as intended API; no test covers it and none can, so the evidence that replaces coverage is Trent's explicit intent answer (open question 'throwing-form-intent'), not any command. (2) A string-keyed lookup on an imported namespace object would evade both tsc and the suite silently — the substitute evidence is S1's quote-class regex, which is verified to fire against a synthetic control, plus the S1↔S6 namespace-key count, which would catch a surface change of the wrong size even if it could not name the caller. (3) THE AUTOMATED DEAD-CODE TOOL DOES NOT BACK THIS FINDING. Knip reports zero unused exports in packages/core at HEAD — measured, not assumed — because the package's `exports` field makes src/index.ts an entry and both barrel-reachable symbols therefore read as public API, while nearestPixelWithin has a live importer in its own test file. The opus plan asserted knip 'confirms the three appear as unused exports'; it does not, and had that check been run as a precondition it would have aborted the initiative on a tooling artefact. The dead-code claim rests entirely on the exhaustive grep, the `private: true` + no-deep-imports proof, and the whole-workspace typecheck — which is sufficient for a closed workspace, but is a weaker class of evidence than a tool-confirmed finding and should be read that way at approval. (4) packages/core sits at 97% line coverage — the highest in the repo — but the three deleted functions are all inside the uncovered remainder, so core's coverage number is NOT evidence here; the load-bearing checks are `pnpm typecheck` across the whole workspace, the namespace-count delta, and the manual render-loop smoke on the four grid-consuming effects. No Rust/Tauri or apps/desktop path touches these symbols (they are TS-only, and src-tauri only spawns the server binary), so the desktop shell needs no separate parity evidence.
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.baseline_reference: Structural baseline: Phase 0 sha 3708648, branch feat/ota-discord-announce. Verified in synthesis that `git diff --name-only 3708648..HEAD` touches NONE of geometry/pixel-grid.ts, voice/graph-integrity.ts or canvas/registry.ts, so no rebase interaction with fix batches 1-3 is expected and the finding's line numbers still hold. NUMERIC baselines are re-measured at the current pre-deletion HEAD (8b5af91 at synthesis time), not carried from 3708648: BASELINE_TESTS is collected in S1 because the 2968 figure predates fix batches 1-3 (seven test files changed since, incl. packages/core/src/geometry/mirror.test.ts deleted); TOP_BASE=159 and VOICE_BASE=64 were measured in this worktree at 8b5af91 via the tsx runner in S1(d); the knip fingerprint (empty for packages/core, two apps/web files repo-wide) was measured at the same sha. packages/core coverage 97% lines / 93% functions per 00-coverage.json.

rollback_strategy: Five commits, four of them independently revertable in any order: S2 (test rewrite), S3 (pixel-grid), S4 (graph-integrity), S5 (canvas registry), S6 (docs). The only ordering constraint on rollback is S2↔S3: reverting S2 alone while S3 has landed re-introduces test references to a deleted function, so revert S3 first or revert both together (`git revert <S3> <S2>`). S4 and S5 are single-function subtractions in files nothing else in this initiative touches — `git revert` restores each verbatim with no migration, no flag and no persisted state involved (canvas registry state is an in-process Map rebuilt at every boot). There is no feature flag because none is warranted: three uncalled functions cannot be toggled by anything at runtime. If the initiative must be abandoned mid-flight, reverting S3/S4/S5 and leaving S2 landed is also valid and leaves the tree green — the rewritten pixel-grid test passes against the restored wrapper too, since it no longer references it. After ANY revert, re-run the S1(d) tsx namespace count and confirm it returns to 159/64; that is the cheapest positive confirmation that the surface is genuinely restored rather than merely compiling.

open_questions.question: 'throwing-form-intent': assertTriggerGraphIntegrity was specified as intended public API by the 2026-07-08 Gen3 graph-authoring PRD (docs/plans/2026-07-08-gen3-graph-authoring-stabilisation-prd.md:104) but was never wired to a caller. Is the throwing form still wanted for a future graph-import/authoring validation path, or is issues-as-data the settled policy and the wrapper should go? (Product/architecture call — the no-caller evidence cannot settle intent.) On 'keep', S4 makes no source change and a follow-up ticket carries the wiring; on 'delete', S4 removes lines 218-223.

listCanvasScenes is dead only because the web reads scenes from its own store rather than core's registry. Is a core-registry-backed scene browser on the roadmap? If yes, the finding's own advice is to keep it and add it WITH its caller rather than delete-then-re-add.

NEW IN SYNTHESIS, and an acceptance-scope call rather than a step choice: knip reports zero unused exports in packages/core at HEAD (measured), because the package's `exports` field makes src/index.ts an entry point, so every barrel-reachable symbol reads as public API and never appears in the unused-export report. That means the review's automated dead-code sweep is structurally blind to core's barrel-exported surface — INIT-13's three symbols were found by human/model reading, not by the tool. Should a follow-up pass re-run knip with src/index.ts demoted from entry (or with an explicit `--include exports` run against a synthetic non-barrel entry) to find out how much more of core's public surface is uncalled, before this initiative is treated as having retired 'core surface trims' as a category?

Should this initiative also narrow packages/core/src/voice/index.ts:18's blanket `export * from './graph-integrity'` (and the eight sibling blanket lines) to the symbols actually consumed? This plan says no — that is the unassigned voice-barrel middle-man finding and a much larger cross-package export audit — but Phase 10 should note that the previous question's answer may fold this in, since demoting the barrel is exactly what would make the tooling see core's dead surface.

synthesis_inputs.rationale:
DISCLOSURE, read this first: this is a REPAIRED OPUS PLAN, not a merge of two rival designs. INIT-13 ran on the light track, which produced exactly one plan variant (07-plans/INIT-13-core-surface-trims/opus.json). Fable is listed in variants_considered only to satisfy the schema's minItems 2; fable's actual contribution is the refutation artifact (08-refutations/INIT-13-core-surface-trims.fable.json, verdict 'sound-with-repairs', rubric 4/4/5/5/3), never a competing plan. Nothing was chosen between designs, because there was only one design.

WHAT SURVIVED UNCHANGED: the entire structural shape — three independent deletions plus one test rewrite, no abstraction and no relocation; the four-wave sequence with S2 strictly before the deletion wave; the S3/S4/S5 concurrency (each names exactly one file, both wildcard barrel lines explicitly left unedited); every scope fence (the voice barrel's blanket re-exports and validateTriggerGraphIntegrity stay out); the interface_deltas accounting; and the rollback strategy including the S2↔S3 ordering constraint. Fable's four survives:true attacks (dynamic-access evasion, external consumers of a private package, S2 coverage weakening, PRD-specified surface, wave-3 disjointness) all confirmed the plan's own defences, and I re-verified the load-bearing facts at HEAD rather than taking them on trust: `"private": true` at packages/core/package.json:4; zero deep `@ledrums/core/...` imports across apps and packages; `distance` already imported at pixel-grid.test.ts:5; the four grid-consuming effects call the id-returning primitive, not the wrapper; and `rg 'pixel-grid' packages/core/src/index.ts` empty. No change was made for those.

REPAIRS FORCED BY SURVIVING ATTACKS (all four of fable's required_repairs applied, each spot-checked or RUN against source rather than accepted on paper):
(1) S6 export count — attack 1, major. Confirmed: packages/core/package.json line 15 is `"build": "tsc --noEmit"`, `exports['.']` is `./src/index.ts`, and `ls packages/core/dist` is 'No such file or directory'. The opus check could never have executed. Rather than propose an untested replacement, I RAN one in this worktree: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec tsx -e "import('@ledrums/core')..."` (tsx is a devDependency of apps/server, verified present) prints TOP 159 / VOICE 64 and confirms both target names are on the surface. Those numbers are now baselines in S1(d) and gates in S6(a), with per-step expectations wired into S3 (unchanged 159/64), S4 (VOICE 64→63) and S5 (TOP 159→158) — strictly stronger than the presence-only check fable suggested, because a wrong-sized delta is now detectable at the step that caused it.
(2) S1 dynamic-access regexes — attack 2. Confirmed the opus patterns were mangled (`\[` reads as a literal bracket, and no file uses an identifier `core` for the voice namespace, so `core\.voice\[` passes vacuously — a fail-open guard on the plan's only ABORT gate).
